'''Neil William Ashcroft''' (27 November 1938 – 15 March 2021) was a British [[Solid-state physics|solid-state]] [[physicist]].

==Early life and education==
Ashcroft was born in [[London]] on 27 November 1938, and migrated to New Zealand in 1947.<ref name="DomPost death notice">{{cite news |url=https://deaths.dompost.co.nz/obituaries/dominion-post-nz/obituary.aspx?n=neil-ashcroft&pid=198165093 |title=Neil Ashcroft death notice |date=27 March 2021 |work=Dominion Post |access-date=27 March 2021}}</ref> He was educated at [[Hutt Valley High School]], and completed his undergraduate studies at [[Victoria University of Wellington|Victoria University College]],<ref name="DomPost death notice"/> earning a Bachelor of Science degree, in 1958. He received his [[PhD]] in 1964 from the [[University of Cambridge]] for research investigating the [[Fermi surface]]s of metals.<ref name=ashphd>{{cite thesis|degree=PhD|publisher=University of Cambridge|title=The Fermi surface and transport properties of metals|first=Neil William|last=Ashcroft|date=1965|url=http://ethos.bl.uk/OrderDetails.do?uin=uk.bl.ethos.596179|oclc=13919109|archive-date=29 July 2023|access-date=23 June 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230729012151/https://ethos.bl.uk/OrderDetails.do?uin=uk.bl.ethos.596179|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.aip.org/history/acap/biographies/bio.jsp?ashcroftn |title=Biography of Neil Ashcroft from the American Physical Society |access-date=18 December 2012 |archive-date=23 June 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150623234225/http://www.aip.org/history/acap/biographies/bio.jsp?ashcroftn |url-status=dead }}</ref>

==Career==
Following his PhD, Ashcroft completed [[postdoctoral research]] at the [[University of Chicago]] and at [[Cornell University]], where he became a professor in 1975.  In 1990 he was named the Horace White Professor of Physics, and was elected to emeritus status in 2006.

He served as the director for the Laboratory of Atomic and Solid State Physics at Cornell University (1979–1984), the director for the Cornell Center for Materials Research (1997–2000), and as the deputy director for the High Energy Synchrotron Source (1990–1997).<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20120130214401/http://www.physics.cornell.edu/professorspeople/professors/?page=website/faculty&action=show/id=54 Cornell Physics faculty biography]</ref>

Between 1986 and 1987, he served as the head of the Condensed Matter division of the [[American Physical Society]]. His [[Ashcroft and Mermin|textbook on solid-state physics]], written with [[N. David Mermin]], is a standard text in the field.<ref>''Solid State Physics.'' Holt, Rinehart and Winston, New York NY u. a. 1976, {{ISBN|0-03-049346-3}} .</ref><ref>{{cite journal|author=Smoluchowski, R.|title=Review: ''Solid State Physics'' by N. W. Ashcroft and N. D. Mermin|journal=Physics Today|volume=30|issue=1|date=January 1977|pages=61–65|url=http://www.physicstoday.org/resource/1/phtoad/v30/i1/p61_s2?bypassSSO=1|doi=10.1063/1.3037370|doi-access=free}}</ref>

Ashcroft died in [[Ithaca, New York]], on 15 March 2021.<ref name="DomPost death notice"/>

==Awards and honours==
In 1997, Ashcroft was elected to the U.S. [[National Academy of Sciences]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.nasonline.org/directory-entry/n-w-ashcroft-zpjrgn/ |title=Member Directory |publisher=National Academy of Sciences |access-date=2021-03-15}}</ref>

In 2003, he was awarded the [[Bridgman Award]] for his contributions to [[high-pressure physics]]. Since that date, he was therefore an honorary member of the [[AIRAPT]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.airapt.org |title=AIRAPT, International Association for the Advancement of High Pressure Science and Technology |publisher=AIRAPT |accessdate=2021-03-17}}</ref>
